precepts.text: The house of Israel will bury Gog and all his multitude for seven months to cleanse the land, so much death that the passengers set up signs by the bones for the buriers.
precepts.point: The Most High is going to lay His vengeance upon Edom by the hand of His people Israel, His battle axe, and there will be so much death that everyone has to pitch in and bury them for seven months. That is a beautiful thing.

note.label: Psalm 58: The Righteous Shall Rejoice When He Seeth the Vengeance

precepts.why:
“Therefore, thou son of man, prophesy against Gog, and say, Thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I am against thee, O Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal”. When the vengeance comes, “I will give unto Gog a place there of graves in Israel, the valley of the passengers on the east of the sea: and it shall stop the noses of the passengers: and there shall they bury Gog and all his multitude: and they shall call it The valley of Hamon–gog.”

“And seven months shall the house of Israel be burying of them, that they may cleanse the land. Yea, all the people of the land shall bury them; and it shall be to them a renown the day that I shall be glorified, saith the Lord God.” There will be so much death that everyone has to pitch in and bury them for seven months. They sever out men of continual employment to pass through the land and bury those that remain, and “when any seeth a man’s bone, then shall he set up a sign by it, till the buriers have buried it in the valley of Hamon–gog.”

The righteous rejoice when they see that vengeance, and it is a renown to Israel the day the Most High is glorified. That is a beautiful thing, and a man shall say, verily he is a God that judgeth in the earth.

precepts.text: The armies gathered with Gog are named, Persia, Ethiopia, Libya, Gomer, and Togarmah, showing Esau conspiring to draw all the other nations to come against Israel.
precepts.point: This is the same setting as Revelation 20, when Satan is loosed in both the spiritual and the physical form: the spiritual demon Satan and the physical Esau. The Most High smites the bow out of Gog's left hand and causes his arrows to fall out of his right hand, so no weapon formed against Israel will prosper. He smacks their weapons out of their hand and their weapon is for naught.

note.label: Ezekiel 39: The Fall of Gog and the Gathering of Israel

precepts.why:
Gog is “the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal”, and Magog is the land of Russia. Whoever comes out of the land of southern Georgia and Russia we know from the scriptures is Esau. Chapter 38 sets it up: the Most High sets His face against “Gog, the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal”, and says “I will turn thee back, and put hooks into thy jaws, and I will bring thee forth, and all thine army, horses and horsemen, all of them clothed with all sorts of armour, even a great company with bucklers and shields, all of them handling swords”.

Then the armies gathered with him are named: “Persia, Ethiopia, and Libya with them; all of them with shield and helmet: Gomer, and all his bands; the house of Togarmah of the north quarters, and all his bands: and many people with thee.” That is Esau conspiring to draw all the other nations to come against Israel.

This is all prophecy, going forward to the time after Christ has taken down the other nations, when Israel will be in their land. He brings Gog up from the north parts upon the mountains of Israel, leaves but the sixth part of him, and smites the bow out of his left hand and the arrows out of his right, so no weapon formed against Israel will prosper.

precepts.text: Satan being loosed at the end of the thousand years is the same moment this prophecy against Gog describes.
precepts.point: This is the same setting as Revelation 20, when Satan is loosed in both the spiritual and the physical form: the spiritual demon Satan and the physical Esau. The Most High smites the bow out of Gog's left hand and causes his arrows to fall out of his right hand, so no weapon formed against Israel will prosper. He smacks their weapons out of their hand and their weapon is for naught.

note.label: Ezekiel 39: The Fall of Gog and the Gathering of Israel

precepts.why:
“And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison”. That is the same moment this prophecy against Gog describes: after Christ has taken down the other nations and Israel is in their land.

Satan is loosed in both the spiritual and the physical form: the spiritual demon Satan, and the physical Esau, Gog the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, coming up from the north parts upon the mountains of Israel.

And the Most High is against him. He smites the bow out of Gog's left hand and causes his arrows to fall out of his right hand. He smacks their weapons out of their hand and their weapon is for naught; no weapon formed against Israel will prosper.

precepts.text: The heathen are gathered to the valley of Jehoshaphat where the Most High sits to judge, the reverse of beating weapons into farm tools.
precepts.point: Israel takes no wood out of the field because they burn the weapons for fuel, and they spoil those that spoiled them and rob those that robbed them. It is a turning: those who took from us, we take from them.

note.label: Ezekiel 39: The Fall of Gog and the Gathering of Israel

precepts.why:
Joel gives the gathering that ends this way: “Proclaim ye this among the Gentiles; Prepare war, wake up the mighty men, let all the men of war draw near; let them come up”. The heathen are gathered to the valley of Jehoshaphat where the Most High sits to judge. It is the reverse of beating weapons into farm tools; the Gentiles are told to prepare war.

And this is what becomes of their war. “Behold, it is come, and it is done”; those that dwell in the cities of Israel go forth and burn the weapons, “the shields and the bucklers, the bows and the arrows, and the handstaves, and the spears”, with fire seven years. Their weapons are taken from them. They will be beaten into submission and forced to work the land instead of making war.

Israel takes no wood out of the field because they burn the weapons for fuel, and “they shall spoil those that spoiled them, and rob those that robbed them”. It is a turning: those who took from us, we take from them.

precepts.text: Israel's gates stand open continually so the forces and wealth of the gentiles may be brought in and their kings serve as servants.
precepts.point: Israel takes no wood out of the field because they burn the weapons for fuel, and they spoil those that spoiled them and rob those that robbed them. It is a turning: those who took from us, we take from them.

note.label: Ezekiel 39: The Fall of Gog and the Gathering of Israel

precepts.why:
“they shall spoil those that spoiled them, and rob those that robbed them”. Isaiah shows the same turning: “thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought.”

Israel's gates stand open continually so the forces and wealth of the Gentiles may be brought in, and their kings serve as servants. The mighty men who came up against Israel have their shields, bows, arrows, handstaves and spears burned for fuel seven years; beaten into submission, they work the land instead of making war.

Those who took from us, we take from them. Their weapons become our firewood and their wealth comes in through our open gates.

precepts.text: Israel is the people the Most High formed for Himself to show forth His praise, which is fulfilled as they return to His law before the nations.
precepts.point: He gathers them out of their enemies' land, as we are being gathered today from the four corners of the earth, and He is sanctified in them in the sight of many nations. The heathen had nothing to do with our captivity; it was the Lord's will, and no one can resist the will of the Lord. He leaves none of them among the heathen anymore, and He will not hide His face anymore, for He has poured out His spirit upon the house of Israel.

note.label: Ezekiel 39: The Fall of Gog and the Gathering of Israel

precepts.why:
“This people have I formed for myself; they shall shew forth my praise.” Israel is the people the Most High formed for Himself, and that is why He brings again the captivity of Jacob and has mercy upon the whole house of Israel, upon those who repent and endure to the end. He is jealous for His holy name.

He gathers them out of their enemies' lands, as we are being gathered today from the four corners of the earth, and is “sanctified in them in the sight of many nations”. As they return to His law before the nations, they show forth His praise. Then they know that He is the Lord their God, “which caused them to be led into captivity among the heathen”. The heathen had nothing to do with our captivity; it was the Lord's will, and no one can resist the will of the Lord.

He has gathered them to their own land and “left none of them any more there”. He will not hide His face any more, for He has poured out His spirit upon the house of Israel: the people formed for Himself, showing forth His praise.

precepts.text: The Most High pours out his spirit upon the house of Israel and hides his face no more from them.
precepts.point: While Peter yet spake, the Holy Ghost fell on all who heard, and they of the circumcision were astonished that on the "Gentiles" also the gift was poured out, for they spake with tongues and magnified the Most High. The Spirit is poured only on the house of Israel, so the Gentiles receiving it are the children of Israel, the northern kingdom.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word.” They of the circumcision were astonished, “because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost.”

But the Spirit is poured only on the house of Israel: “Neither will I hide my face any more from them: for I have poured out my spirit upon the house of Israel, saith the Lord God.” So the Gentiles receiving it are the children of Israel, the northern kingdom. The Most High hid his face from them no more.

note.label: Ezekiel 39: The Fall of Gog and the Gathering of Israel

points: The Most High tells Ezekiel to speak to every feathered fowl and every beast of the field to gather to His sacrifice upon the mountains of Israel, that they may eat flesh and drink blood. There will be a great slaughter in that day.

note.label: Ezekiel 39: The Fall of Gog and the Gathering of Israel

points: They eat the flesh of the mighty and drink the blood of the princes of the earth, of rams, lambs, goats, and bullocks, until they are full and drunken at His table with horses, chariots, and all men of war.

note.label: Ezekiel 39: The Fall of Gog and the Gathering of Israel

points: The Most High sets His glory among the heathen, and all the heathen see the judgment He has executed. Right now the Lord is not glorified in this kingdom, but in that day He will be, and He gets His people's attention. Today the world calls the heathen's works great, their space programs and their weapons of mass destruction, but when the Most High shuts all that down we will realize who the real power is.

note.label: Ezekiel 39: The Fall of Gog and the Gathering of Israel

points: From that day the house of Israel knows that He is the Lord their God, and the heathen know that Israel went into captivity for their iniquity, because they trespassed against Him. That is why we are in the position we are in; He hid His face and gave us into the hand of our enemies because we did not obey.
